newsitem.title: MEXICO: Bomb injures three in botched Mexican bank robbery.
newsitem.headline: Bomb injures three in botched Mexican bank robbery.

text.p: Three people were seriously injured on Monday when a nervous bank robber detonated a briefcase of dynamite during a botched bank hold-up in Mexico City, police said.
"They're very serious injuries," said Francisco Javier Padron Romero, a policeman at the scene of the explosion. He said at least two of the injured looked as if they may die.

He said the robber threatened to trigger the electric detonator unless he was handed over money. But before bank employees could react, he panicked and detonated the briefcase, injuring himself and two bank employees.
"The person must be sick in the head," Padron Romero said.

The hold-up attempt, in a Banamex branch in the south of Mexico City, was the latest in a long-running rash of bank robberies that has plagued Mexico since its 1994-1995 peso crisis and severe recession.
